# opencode-claude-auth-custom

OpenCode plugin that authenticates with your **Claude Code OAuth credentials**
(reusing the subscription you already pay for) while routing requests through a
custom proxy such as **LiteLLM**.

This is a bundled, drop-in variant of `opencode-claude-auth` that additionally
honors two environment variables:

| Variable | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | Overrides the default `https://api.anthropic.com/v1`. Point it at your proxy (e.g. `https://litellm.example.com/v1`). |
| `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS` | Extra headers sent on every request, **without** disturbing the OAuth `Authorization` header. Accepts JSON (`{"x-litellm-api-key":"Bearer sk-..."}`), `key: value`, or `key=value` lines. |

The OAuth bearer token from your Claude Code credentials is still attached
automatically — only the destination and extra headers change.

## Usage

In `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "plugin": ["npm:opencode-claude-auth-custom"]
}
```

## Environment variables

| Variable | Required | Format | Example |
|----------|----------|--------|---------|
| `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | Yes | Full proxy base URL, **including `/v1`** | `https://litellm.example.com/v1` |
| `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS` | Yes\* | One of: JSON (`{"key":"value"}`), `key: value`, or `key=value`. Multiple headers: one per line. | `x-litellm-api-key: Bearer sk-example123` |
| `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` | No | Exact Anthropic model name (see note below) | `claude-sonnet-5` |

\* `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS` is only required when your proxy needs it (LiteLLM does).

### Full example

```bash
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="https://litellm.example.com/v1"
export ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS="x-litellm-api-key: Bearer sk-example123"
export ANTHROPIC_MODEL="claude-sonnet-5"
```

### Minimal example (omit ANTHROPIC_MODEL)

```bash
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="https://litellm.example.com/v1"
export ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS="x-litellm-api-key: Bearer sk-example123"
```

Restart opencode and the Claude models will be available through your proxy.

## LiteLLM proxy configuration

> This plugin does the same as the official LiteLLM guide for Claude Code
> ([Using Claude Code Max Subscription](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/tutorials/claude_code_max_subscription)),
> but for OpenCode instead of the Claude CLI.

Your LiteLLM `config.yaml` **must** enable header forwarding so the OAuth token
from your Claude Code credentials reaches the Anthropic API:

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: claude-sonnet-5
    litellm_params:
      model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5
  # ...other models you want to expose

general_settings:
  forward_client_headers_to_llm_api: true  # Required: forwards OAuth token to Anthropic
```

Why `forward_client_headers_to_llm_api`? This forwards the request's
`Authorization` header (the OAuth bearer token from Claude Code) through LiteLLM
to the Anthropic API. Without it, Anthropic rejects the request. The
`x-litellm-api-key` header (from `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS`) is still used by
LiteLLM for authentication, tracking, budgets and rate limits.

## Model names

> ⚠️ Model names must match the **Anthropic** model names exactly (e.g.
> `claude-sonnet-5`, `claude-opus-4`, `claude-haiku-4`). Do **not** use the name
> that LiteLLM exposes externally — the plugin rewrites the request path toward
> your proxy, so the model identifier reaching the proxy should be the real
> Anthropic one, and that model must be available in your LiteLLM configuration.
>
> `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` is **optional**. If omitted, opencode uses its default model.

## Notes

This package ships a single self-contained `opencode-claude-auth-custom.js`
bundle. It requires `@opencode-ai/plugin` as a peer dependency (provided by
opencode itself).
